record.context_brief: Central lozenge probability in a semiregular hexagon
record.original_question: In the semiregular hexagon with side lengths 2n-1, 2n, 2n-1, 2n, 2n-1, 2n, prove that the central location consisting of the two innermost triangles is covered by a lozenge in exactly one-third of all lozenge tilings. Equivalently, in the dual honeycomb graph, prove that a uniformly random perfect matching contains the central edge with probability exactly 1/3.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Show that in the 2n − 1, 2n, 2n − 1 semiregular hexagon, the central location (consisting of the two innermost triangles) is covered by a lozenge in exactly one-third of the tilings.
(Equivalently: Show that if one chooses a random perfect matching of the dual graph, the probability that the central edge is contained in the matching is exactly 1/3.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the semiregular hexagon $H_n$ in the triangular lattice whose six side lengths, in cyclic order, are $2n-1,\ 2n,\ 2n-1,\ 2n,\ 2n-1,\ 2n$. A lozenge (or rhombus) is the union of two unit equilateral triangles of the triangular lattice that share an edge, and a lozenge tiling of $H_n$ is a covering of $H_n$ by such lozenges with disjoint interiors. Equivalently, lozenge tilings of $H_n$ are in bijection with perfect matchings of the dual honeycomb graph $G_n$ whose vertices are the unit triangles of $H_n$ and whose edges connect adjacent triangles.

By the symmetry of $H_n$, there is a unique pair of unit triangles forming a lozenge at the very center; call this central lozenge $\ell^*$, and let $e^*$ be the corresponding central edge of $G_n$.

Prove that, when a lozenge tiling of $H_n$ is chosen uniformly at random (equivalently, when a perfect matching of $G_n$ is chosen uniformly at random),
$$\Pr[\ell^* \text{ appears in the tiling}] \;=\; \Pr[e^* \in \text{the matching}] \;=\; \tfrac{1}{3},$$
for every positive integer $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the central lozenge appears in exactly one third of all lozenge tilings of the semiregular hexagon with sides 2n−1, 2n, 2n−1, 2n, 2n−1, 2n was proved by Ciucu and Krattenthaler ("The number of centered lozenge tilings of a symmetric hexagon", arXiv:math/9712209, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A), via Gessel–Viennot determinants and explicit product formulas; further refinements were given by Fulmek and Krattenthaler. The problem is therefore solved.

status_evidence.title: The number of centered lozenge tilings of a symmetric hexagon
status_evidence.snippet: Ciucu and Krattenthaler prove Propp's conjecture that the number of centered lozenge tilings of the semiregular hexagon equals one third of the total number of tilings.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Rhombus Tilings of a Symmetric Hexagon which Contain a Fixed Rhombus on the Symmetry Axis, II
status_evidence.snippet: Fulmek and Krattenthaler extend the centered-lozenge enumeration to fixed lozenges along the symmetry axis.
status_evidence.claim: Refinements and extensions of the central-lozenge result exist.
